messages.content:
How would the Sun appear to an astronaut on Pluto compared with how it looks from Earth?

A. The Sun would appear larger and brighter.
B. The Sun would appear smaller and brighter.
C. The Sun would appear larger and dimmer.
D. The Sun would appear smaller and dimmer.
只答选项字母

Which activity illustrates the main function of the motor neuron complex?

A. transferring impulses to the appropriate muscle
B. receiving sensory impulses from the environment
C. delivering regular impulses to the autonomic system
D. processing impulses within the cerebral cortex
只答选项字母

On the Galapagos Islands, an iguana that lives in the water is most likely able to survive without competition from an iguana that lives on land because it

A. swims faster.
B. has a larger body.
C. has a tougher scaly skin.
D. has a different food source.
只答选项字母

Which gas could cause a glowing splint to burst into flame?

A. Neon
B. Oxygen
C. Nitrogen
D. Carbon dioxide
只答选项字母

Which activity is an important function of nucleases?

A. repairing the double strand of DNA
B. concentrating RNA into a nucleolus
C. maintaining homeostasis of nucleoplasm
D. dissolving the nuclear membrane during mitosis
只答选项字母

A group of citizens want to have a statue built out of marble. They want to place it in a climate that has a slow rate of chemical weathering. In which type of climate would it be best to place the statue for the slowest rate of chemical weathering?

A. hot and dry
B. cold and dry
C. hot and humid
D. cold and humid
只答选项字母

Which article might appear in a scientific magazine?

A. "The Religions of South America"
B. "The Money Systems of South America"
C. "The Flora and Fauna of South America"
D. "The Political Systems of South America"
只答选项字母

A birdwatcher wants to identify an eastern bluebird. What feature of a bird should the birdwatcher evaluate first to identify an eastern bluebird?

A. beak shape
B. eye position
C. feather pattern
D. tail-feather length
只答选项字母

Scientists are studying the factors that influence the climate of a region. In attempts to gather accurate data, the scientists should use data that includes the

A. number of earthquakes that occur each year.
B. types of organisms in the environment.
C. number of people living in the area.
D. type of weather that has occurred.
只答选项字母

Which of the following involves a learned behavior?

A. laying eggs to reproduce
B. having hollow, light-weight bones
C. avoiding insects that taste bad
D. having white feathers on the throat
只答选项字母

If the results of an experiment do not support the hypothesis, the scientist will most likely do all of the following except

A. check for errors in the experimental procedure.
B. repeat the experiment.
C. change data to support the hypothesis.
D. ask new questions.
只答选项字母

The human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) causes AIDS. The first known human cases AIDS were in Africa in the late 1950s. Since then, tens of millions of people have died from the disease, and tens of millions more people all over the world are infected. Which term best describes the disease AIDS?

A. isolated cases
B. outbreak
C. epidemic
D. pandemic
只答选项字母

Which form of energy is produced when a rubber band vibrates?

1. chemical
2. light
3. electrical
4. sound
只答选项字母

Which part of a sunflower plant absorbs water and nutrients?

A. Roots
B. Stems
C. Leaves
D. Flowers
只答选项字母

Plants that are different from each another may have similar structures. Which structure do all plants have in common?

A. flowers
B. fruit
C. roots
D. trunks
只答选项字母

A wild turkey's forest community includes

A. insects
B. rainfall
C. soil
D. wind
只答选项字母

What force causes objects to be pulled toward Earth?

A. friction
B. gravity
C. light
D. electricity

Which is a fact rather than an opinion about earthquakes?

A. Earthquakes occur along fault lines.
B. Earthquakes are worse than hurricanes.
C. Earthquakes are bad for all local businesses.
D. Earthquakes always cause major damage to homes.

A. 6
B. 12
C. 18
D. 24

Which is a trait that a child can inherit from its parents?

A. eye color
B. a broken leg
C. length of hair
D. language skills
只答选项字母

What happens to colored sugar when it is added to water?

A. The sugar reacts and colors the water.
B. The sugar becomes white and the water changes color.
C. The sugar evaporates and the water changes color.
D. The sugar dissolves and colors the water.
只答选项字母

What are the properties of the Earth's crust and mantle that are most responsible for Earth's tectonic activity?

A. They are in different states and have different temperatures.
B. They are in the same state but have different temperatures.
C. They are in different states but have the same temperature.
D. They are the same state and have the same temperature.
只答选项字母

From what source does almost all heat energy on Earth come?

A. Wind
B. Water
C. The Sun
D. The Moon

The energy that allows the water cycle to occur comes from

A. friction.
B. electricity.
C. the Sun.
D. radioactive decay.

The boiling point of water in degrees Celsius is

A. 0°C.
B. 32°C.
C. 100°C.
D. 212°C.
只答选项字母

In a laboratory procedure, students added sodium hydroxide crystals to a beaker of water and allowed the resulting solution to cool. Based on this information, which type of chemical process most likely occurred?

A. electrical
B. energetic
C. exothermic
D. endothermic
只答选项字母

Which of these situations would most likely be a result of climate change?

A. weaker storms, causing less shoreline erosion
B. shorter days, causing longer hibernation periods
C. shrinking glaciers, causing sea levels to rise
D. increased radioactivity, causing damage to cells
只答选项字母

Blood is a fluid made up of several different parts. What level of structural organization best describes blood?

A. a cell
B. a tissue
C. an organ
D. a system
只答选项字母

Use the information to answer the question. Over the last 150 years, the use of fossil fuels has increased, resulting in more carbon dioxide and other greenhouse gases in the atmosphere. Some scientists think that these atmospheric gases will result in global warming. Scientists have recorded data on global temperature changes and have predicted possible changes in sea level that may affect Maryland residents. Using fossil fuels in the United States will most likely contribute to rising sea levels globally by

A. increasing oxygen levels
B. decreasing oxygen levels
C. increasing carbon dioxide levels
D. decreasing carbon dioxide levels
只答选项字母

Which of these tools is best for recording observations outdoors?

A. a ruler
B. a graph
C. a notebook
D. a calculator
只答选项字母

A large plant population may impose selective pressure on a smaller, isolated group of plants, resulting in a change in allele distribution. Which mechanism is responsible for this change in the allele distribution?

A. mutation
B. hybridization
C. genetic drift
D. trait acquisition
只答选项字母

The first powerful telescopes were built during the early 1600s. Scientists at that time were able to learn more about which subject by using the telescope?

A. the shape of continents of Earth
B. the effect of storms and hurricanes
C. forces changing the surface of Earth
D. planets and moons in the solar system
只答选项字母

Which of the following colors of visible light has the longest wavelength?

A. red
B. blue
C. green
D. orange
只答选项字母

Some scientists believe that the mass extinction of dinosaurs was caused by the impact of a large meteorite on Earth. This impact would have caused a darkening of the sky due to dust blown into the upper atmosphere. This darkening would have reduced the sizes of some ecosystems because of

A. longer seasons.
B. accelerated erosion.
C. reduced photosynthesis.
D. increased number of hurricanes.
只答选项字母

A geologist found several types of seashell fossils in a rock layer. Which is the best conclusion about the rock layer?

A. The rock was once buried under a swamp.
B. Water from a river washed across the rock.
C. The rock was once sediment at the bottom of an ocean.
D. Migrating animals dropped the seashell into the rock.
只答选项字母

What is the green pigment that allows plants to change the Sun's energy into chemical energy?

A. glucose
B. chlorophyll
C. mitochondria
D. photosynthesis
只答选项字母

In New England, there are noticeable patterns of seasonal change. Which information could you collect to BEST illustrate this change?

A. air temperature
B. wind speed
C. amount of precipitation
D. number of cloudy days
只答选项字母

Which statement describes a characteristic of both sexual and asexual reproduction?

A. The processes require egg cells.
B. New cells are produced.
C. Two parents are required.
D. The processes produce genetically unique offspring.
只答选项字母

The water cycle requires energy. The main source of energy for the water cycle is

A. wind
B. gravity
C. the sun
D. the moon
只答选项字母

Which of the following units best represents the density of an object?

A. kg
B. hr
C. m/s^2
D. g/cm^3
只答选项字母

Which is a characteristic of sedimentary rock?

A. forms in layers
B. looks very shiny
C. contains crystals
D. forms from magma
只答选项字母

The Moon revolves around Earth about once every

A. day.
B. year.
C. week.
D. month.
只答选项字母

How often does Earth rotate on its axis?

A. once every 12 hours
B. once every 24 hours
C. once every month
D. once every year
只答选项字母

Which current property of our solar system is mainly due to solar emissions occurring soon after the initiation of fusion in the Sun's core?

A. directions of revolution of the planets
B. directions of rotation of the planets
C. distribution of moons among the planets
D. distribution of elements among the planets
只答选项字母

Which material is the best conductor of electricity?

A. metal
B. glass
C. wood
D. plastic
只答选项字母

A ball rolling on the ground is observed to slow down and stop. Based on Newton's first law of motion, what is the best conclusion?

A. An object in motion eventually stops.
B. The ball must have been going slightly uphill.
C. The ball did not have enough mass to keep going.
D. There must have been an outside force acting on the ball.
只答选项字母

Students wanted to see if the growth of a plant was affected by using four different types of soil. How should the students best carry out this investigation after potting the plants in the four different types of soil?

A. observe the plants and record observations daily
B. move the plants to new locations every day
C. measure the height of each plant every hour
D. add different amounts of water to each plant
只答选项字母

Some processes that shape Earth's surface are slow. Other processes are rapid. Which statement describes a rapid change?

A. Glaciers melt and form rivers.
B. Wind weathers rocks into sand.
C. Earthquakes move land and rocks.
D. Rivers carry sediment and build deltas.
只答选项字母

In which of these organs does most absorption of nutrients take place?

A. liver
B. stomach
C. small intestine
D. large intestine
只答选项字母

A group of fish was released into a local lake. This species of fish had never lived in the lake before. Scientists want to collect data on how the lake's ecosystem is affected by the new fish. Which method of data collection will give the most accurate results?

A. Measuring oxygen levels in the lake for two months
B. Checking the lake water for nutrient levels on one day
C. Sampling fish populations in the lake over several years
D. Observing the surface of the lake for signs of the new fish after one week
只答选项字母

Which type of storm causes the most flooding in areas located near an ocean coastline?

A. Tornado
B. Hurricane
C. Blizzard
D. Freezing rain
只答选项字母

What information about stars can be learned by using a spectrometer?

A. chemical composition
B. distance from Earth
C. size
D. speed
只答选项字母

Which of the following statements best describes the role of gravity in the formation of stars?

A. Gravity converts solid matter into gases and light energy.
B. Gravity causes gases and dust particles to condense into spheres.
C. Gravity cools gases and liquids until they become one solid mass.
D. Gravity pushes rocks and dust particles outward from a dense center.
只答选项字母

A small aluminum cube is dropped into a beaker of water to determine the buoyancy. Which of these is not necessary in determining the buoyant force acting on the cube?

A. density of water
B. displaced volume
C. gravitational pull on Earth
D. density of the aluminum cube
只答选项字母

Which two theories of Moon formation propose that much or all of the material comprising the Moon came from Earth?

A. The Fission Theory and The Coaccretion Theory
B. The Coaccretion Theory and The Capture Theory
C. The Fission Theory and the Giant Impact Theory
D. The Capture Theory and the Giant Impact Theory
只答选项字母

An unusual type of fossil clam is found in rock layers high in the Swiss Alps. The same type of fossil clam is also found in the Rocky Mountains of North America. From this, scientists conclude that

A. glaciers carried the fossils up the mountains
B. the Rocky Mountains and the Swiss Alps are both volcanic in origin
C. clams once lived in mountains, but have since evolved into sea-dwelling creatures
D. the layers of rocks in which the fossils were found are from the same geologic age
只答选项字母

Clownfish take shelter in the tentacles of sea anemones and keep sea anemones clean. Which type of relationship does this represent?

A. parasitism
B. commensalism
C. mutualism
D. neutralism

Which of the following is the best example of a part of the propulsion system of a tractor?

A. engine
B. front headlight
C. hood
D. steering wheel
只答选项字母

Which rankings of trees would most likely useful in a scientific study of fruit production in apple trees?

A. date of flowering and the fruit yield
B. fruit yield and taste of the fruit
C. taste of the fruit and smell of the flower
D. date of flowering and smell of the flower
只答选项字母

What does a fire take away from a forest that squirrels need to survive?

A. food and soil
B. food and shelter
C. water and soil
D. water and shelter

Increasing and revising scientific knowledge of different types of bacteria will most likely enable scientists to develop ways to

A. help patients spend less time in the emergency room.
B. aid research students who are studying complex organisms.
C. help make medicines from newly discovered plants.
D. develop specialized antibiotics that are directed at single-celled organisms.
只答选项字母

Which characteristic of a cold-water upwelling near the coast of Northern California results in a large concentration of marine organisms?

A. loss of thermal stability
B. high nutrient concentration
C. consistent surface-current flow rate
D. increased availability of dissolved oxygen

A student measured liquid with a graduated cylinder. Which of the following units could be used to record the volume of the liquid?

A. pounds
B. meters
C. grams
D. milliliters

Which term best describes the process responsible for cave formation that results from rock being dissolved by groundwater?

A. chemical weathering
B. glacial movement
C. sedimentation

In a cell, a newly synthesized protein requires modification by the addition of a carbohydrate. Which structure will transport the protein from the site of synthesis to the site of modification?

A. a ribosome
B. the endoplasmic reticulum
C. the Golgi apparatus

A. a nucleus

In order for electricity from a battery to power a light bulb, the wire has to provide the electricity a path to do what?

A. condensation

Which structure is found in a plant cell but not in an animal cell?

1. cell wall

The ichthyornis was a type of bird that lived over 65 million years ago. It lived near the sea and hunted for fish over the water. Fossils have been found in Kansas, many miles from the present-day ocean. Which cause of extinction is most likely to be found in the fossil record along with ichthyornis fossils?

A. changes in the environment
B. diseases causing illness

A 13-year-old boy has blue eyes. Which statement concerning his eye color is correct?

A. It is a result of asexual reproduction.
B. It is a result of childhood nutrition.
C. It is an inherited characteristic.
D. It is a personal choice.

Tides on Earth are mostly caused by the gravitational pull of

A. the Sun.
B. stars.
C. the Moon.
D. asteroids.

Which of these is the BEST sign that the fall season has begun?

A. Plants forming new buds
B. Sun shining on flowers
C. Grass being wet in the morning
D. Leaves changing color on trees

A cut to the skin is treated with antiseptic first to avoid

A. an immune response.

A. decreased production cost

If the climate in an area changed over time to become very cold, which change would most likely help a species living there to survive?

A. a thicker neck and longer tail
B. a larger mouth and stronger jaws

As global temperatures increase, certain organisms will be more affected than others. The changes associated with global warming may result in an increase in sea level. Which organisms will be affected most as a result of the change in sea level?

A. birds that eat fish from shallow waters

The best explanation of why carnivores are dependent on plants is because they

A. need to consume plant matter.

Which of these best describes the relationship between Earth's layers?

A. The hottest layers are closest to the core.

A beach is formed when sediment is deposited along a shoreline. What would most likely happen if rivers that empty into the ocean were dammed?

A. Less sediment would be deposited along the shoreline.

C. Sand dunes would become smaller.
D. Deltas would become larger.

When a guitar string is strummed, it produces sound by making

A. air

A. an atom

Which characteristic of an element determines its placement in the periodic table?

A. mass

An increase of carbon dioxide in Earth's atmosphere is most likely to have which effect?

A. decreased variations in day length
B. increased average air temperature

Which energy source could involve a dam?

Which human organ system eliminates liquid and gaseous wastes from the body?

Each layer of Earth has different properties. Which statement best describes the mantle of Earth?

Bile salts play a crucial role in gastrointestinal homeostasis and digestion. Which phrase is the best description of the gastrointestinal function of bile salts?

A. digestion and absorption of proteins in the liver

A class conducts an experiment to determine the best color to paint a solar water heater that they plan to build. For their experimental test, the students have four identical cans. They paint one black, one green, one red, and one white. Each can is filled with 500 mL of 22°C water, and is allowed to sit in the sun for two hours. Which color can will have the greatest increase in water temperature?

In what unit of time does Earth orbit the Sun?

Students go on a field trip to observe salmon spawning in a river. For safety reasons, the students should not

A. explore alone.

If it is determined that the particles in one solid are arranged in a repeating pattern and the particles in another solid are arranged randomly, what must be true about the solids?

A. They are different substances.

Which organisms eat only plants?

A student picked up a small rock using a magnet. The rock probably contained

Grasses, shrubs, and trees are called producers because they make

A scientist observed that the loss of plants near a stream resulted in more soil being washed downstream. How will the excess soil that travels downstream reduce biodiversity?

A. It will destroy the fish habitat.

D. It will introduce an invasive species.

How do plants get water and minerals?

A. absorbed from the soil though the roots
B. absorbed from the soil through the stem

Dr. Wagner is investigating a newly discovered, disease-causing agent. She determines that one structure in the agent is double-stranded RNA. What kind of agent is Dr. Wagner studying?

A. a virus
B. a protist
C. a fungus
D. a bacterium

How many different elements are in the 20 compound sodium carbonate (Na2CO3)?

A. 1
B. 3

D. 7

Which is an example of a hypothesis?

Some jet airplanes fly in a layer of the atmosphere where temperature generally increases with altitude. What is this layer of the atmosphere?

What happens to sugar when it is combined with water?

B. igneous
C. sedimentary

Eagles have strong, sharp beaks that are most likely adapted for the eagle to eat

A. fish.
B. eggs.
C. worms.

A farmer predicts a new sprinkler will keep water from being wasted. What term best describes this prediction?
